assessment: Two narrow tutors, one for each kind of missing piece. Idyllic Tutor ({2}{W}, sorcery) finds an enchantment. The 99 holds eleven: Artist's Talent, Fiery Emancipation, Gratuitous Violence, Jeskai Ascendancy, Knowledge Is Power, Mystic Remora, Rhystic Study, Shark Typhoon, Smothering Tithe, Sorcerer Class and Teferi's Ageless Insight. Stoneforge Mystic ({1}{W}) finds one of four Equipment: Brotherhood Regalia, Embercleave, Lightning Greaves and Robe of Stars. Her {1}{W}, {T} puts an Equipment from your hand onto the battlefield without casting it, which needs a turn of waiting, since it is a tap ability on a creature. Neither tutor finds a commander, a wheel, Consecrated Sphinx, Razorkin Needlehead, Torbran or a shield spell, so neither one makes a keep on its own. Both checker-passed wheel lines on this list run through creatures neither can fetch: Sphinx (stack 009) and Needlehead with Torbran (stack 011). What Idyllic adds to them is a multiplier or a refill. Every combat figure below is oracle arithmetic: no passing stack resolves combat with any card in the 99, so the 21-commander-damage kill stays unproven.

targets.scenario: Turn three or four. No commander yet, two or three lands, no rock, and a commander or a wheel in hand: the game 003 shape, mana-starved for a round.
targets.why: Every opponent draw is a Treasure unless that player pays {2}, so a symmetrical wheel later is seven offers per seat. Tithe has to be on the battlefield before the wheel. No passing stack has Tithe on a board, and the goldfish barely reads its Treasure (treasure engine online by turn 6 in 0.7% of games), so this rests on oracle text. It is a Game Changer and it taxes the whole table, so expect attention.

targets.scenario: Torbran is on the battlefield with Razorkin Needlehead or Brallin beside him (or both), Wheel of Fortune is in hand, and you can wait a turn.
targets.why: It doubles damage from creatures you control, and Needlehead and Brallin are both creatures. Stack 007 settles that each opponent orders the replacements and takes the smaller result: double first, then Torbran's +2, so 4 per ping. Stack 011 is the Wheel under Needlehead and Torbran alone, 21 per seat; with Gratuitous Violence the same seven draws are at least 28 per seat by that arithmetic, before Brallin adds anything. It costs {2}{R}{R}{R}, and red is the short colour at 30 land sources against a target of 36. Needs a stack scenario.

targets.scenario: Shabraz is out at about 10/10 with a clear lane in the air, and you hold a wheel for next turn but no double-strike piece.
targets.why: Creatures you control get +X/+X, where X is the cards drawn this turn. A precombat Windfall for seven puts seven counters on Shabraz (stack 001) and adds at least +7/+7, so a 10/10 attacks as at least a 24/24. By arithmetic that is past 21 in one hit, with no double strike. It costs {3}{W}{U}, so you tutor on one turn and cast the enchantment and the wheel on the next. It is a candidate line in strategic_frame.json and needs a stack scenario.

targets.scenario: The table holds a sorcery-speed sweeper (or has already wiped once), a commander is out or has been removed, and you have nothing to do at instant speed.
targets.why: It is an enchantment, so Idyllic finds it, and few players expect a tutor for a cycler. Hold it and cycle it at an opponent's end step after their wipe. Stack 012: cycling for X=4 is one discard and one draw, which pays Brallin, Marauding Mako and Shabraz a counter each, pings every opponent for 1, and leaves a flying Shark that Brallin's {R} can give trample. The 4/4 size is the card's ruling, taken as an input, not a CR result. Cycling is not casting, so Shu Yun and prowess do not see it. Idyllic is a sorcery, so you tutor on your turn and cycle on theirs.

tutors.notes: Idyllic Tutor is a sorcery for three, so you tutor on one turn and cast on the next. Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation each need {R}{R}{R}, so count your red sources before you name either. Fiery Emancipation is the alternate to Gratuitous Violence: it triples damage from any source you control, Shabraz included, where Torbran never helps him; whether tripled combat damage from a commander counts toward 21 has no stack.

targets.scenario: Default. A commander lands next turn, or has just landed, and the table has shown spot removal.
targets.why: It gives haste and shroud, and equip {0} moves it for free. You named Greaves 'really good' in game 001, the game in which Brallin was removed twice. Shroud also blocks your own targeting, so move Greaves off the commander before you equip anything else or take Shu Yun's double strike.

citations.quote: “Shroud” means “This permanent or player can’t be the target of spells or abilities.”
“Equip [cost]” means “[Cost]: Attach this permanent to target creature you control. Activate only as a sorcery.”

targets.scenario: Behind. A commander has already been removed once (the tax is on), and the table runs exile or bounce that Flawless Maneuver does not stop.
targets.why: For {1}{W} at instant speed the carrier phases out until your next turn. A phased-out permanent is treated as though it does not exist, which answers exile and bounce as well as destroy. Equip {1}. It saves paying the tax again: each recast costs {2} more per earlier cast from the command zone.

citations.quote: If a permanent phases out, its status changes to “phased out.” Except for rules and effects that specifically mention phased-out permanents, a phased-out permanent is treated as though it does not exist.
A commander cast from the command zone costs an additional {2} for each previous time the player casting it has cast it from the command zone that game.

targets.scenario: Closing. Stoneforge has been on the battlefield since your last turn, a commander is at 10/10 or more, and you have {1}{W} plus a lane.
targets.why: Her {1}{W}, {T} puts Embercleave onto the battlefield without paying {4}{R}{R}, and its enter trigger attaches it to target creature you control: +1/+1, double strike, trample. A 10/10 becomes an 11/11 that deals 22 by arithmetic. No passing stack resolves combat with Embercleave, so this is the deck's stated win and it is UNPROVEN. Its equip {3} is a sorcery-speed backup if it falls off. Its trigger targets, so it cannot attach to a commander in Lightning Greaves.

targets.scenario: The board is wide with blockers (game 001's zombie tokens), and Brallin is the commander you have out.
targets.why: Equip legendary creature {1}, and both commanders are legendary. The equipped creature can't be blocked and has ward {2}. Brallin has no evasion of his own, and Shabraz's {W/U} flying grant is the other way over. Ward taxes removal but does not stop it.

tutors.notes: Her ETB is a 'may' search, so you can hold her until you know which of the four you need. The put-onto-battlefield ability needs her untapped and free of summoning sickness.

gaps: No passing stack resolves combat with Embercleave, Knowledge Is Power, Fiery Emancipation or Gratuitous Violence. Every combat figure here is oracle arithmetic (engine.json open_questions[0] and [1]).

Gratuitous Violence on Needlehead's pings (at least 28 per seat from one Wheel) is arithmetic from stacks 007 and 011; no stack holds Needlehead under it. strategic_frame.json lists it as a candidate line, status needs a stack scenario.
Smothering Tithe is on no stack board, and the goldfish's Treasure reading is near zero, so its behind-on-mana value is unmeasured.
Shark Typhoon's draw is not modelled by the goldfish (draw_not_modelled), so the value of fetching it is stack 012 and judgment only.
No artifact measures how often either tutor is cast, or what it found, in a real game. No game is logged on v2.2.0.
